title: xDSL: Sidekick Compilation for SSA-Based Compilers
problem: Compiler researchers face trade-offs: prototyping in production compilers is cumbersome (optimized for speed over simplicity), while new prototype compilers require significant engineering to transition to production.
motivation: Bridging prototype and production compilation enables faster development cycles for compiler research while leveraging production-ready infrastructure for deployment.
method: Introduces sidekick compiler frameworks: multiple interoperable frameworks using textual interchange formats and declarative IR descriptions. Each framework specializes for specific use cases (prototyping, teaching, production). Demonstrates with xDSL, an MLIR sidekick using shared textual IR and IRDL dialect for framework interoperability.
key_novelty: First sidekick compiler framework paradigm enabling seamless interoperability between specialized compilers via textual IR and declarative abstractions.
contributions: Sidekick compiler framework concept for prototyping-to-production workflow
xDSL as MLIR sidekick for teaching and research
Shared textual IR and IRDL dialect for framework exchange
Demonstration on three use cases: teaching, DSL compilation, rewrite systems
limitations: Trade-offs in performance or optimization coverage between frameworks not quantified.
